audience.role: A DSH user who already runs the plugin and is deciding whether to take this version, and a first-time repository reader

checks.note: Both README editions introduce the task checklist, show installation and activation, and explain host compatibility. The changelogs describe version changes without repeating the installation instructions.

The reader can choose the frozen unpublished candidate, install it, inspect and inject the host lock, then enable protection. The compatibility section explicitly identifies rc.1 and rc.2 as separate exact host sets and requires a new session for older Session V2 data.

The README explains the saved checklist and matching tool results before host-lock terminology. The rc.2 addition explains the 33-package set and mixed-version refusal in ordinary language before linking the detailed reference.

The updated paragraphs distinguish registry package identity from native acceptance for an exact artifact and platform. Candidate installation no longer directs the reader to an older published package; publication and real-model acceptance remain separate.

Installation and the visible status command precede detailed contracts. The new compatibility paragraph answers which host versions can be evaluated, with identity mechanics in the reference. The changed changelog bullet states the rc.2 addition first.

The English and Chinese reading paths were read separately. Both provide the same frozen-package command and exact host versions; each explains mixed-version refusal and the need for matching native evidence without relying on the other edition.

findings.message: The structural auditor warns that the status paragraph names exact versions. This is the current compatibility level rather than historical provenance, and the paragraph links docs/COMPATIBILITY.md for the full record of the range, the prerelease rules, and the exact graph. The Chinese edition carries the same warning at README.zh-CN.md:52 and the same link.

limitations: Cold read covered both complete README entry paths and both current 0.5.1 changelog entries; unchanged historical release entries retain their earlier review scope.
Compatibility and local-acceptance references were reconciled for rc.2 and the current validator profile; their historical sections were not re-reviewed end to end.
This receipt binds the reviewed bytes. A later document edit requires fresh review; it does not establish native acceptance, publication or factual correctness.
